draft.title: Making a personal budget
card: A budget is a plan that lists the money you expect to receive (income) and the money you expect to spend (expenses) over a period, such as a month. It keeps spending within income so money can be set aside for a savings goal, such as saving a set amount each week for something you want to buy.
expenses that stay the same each time, such as a phone plan or a gym fee.
expenses that can go up or down, such as snacks, clothes or bus fares.
Subtract total expenses from income to see what is left to save. If expenses are higher than income, the budget shows a shortfall, and you need to cut expenses or earn more.
draft.remember: Income minus all expenses, fixed and variable, shows what is left to save.

a.q: Mia checks what she paid for four things in March and April. Which is a fixed expense?
opts: Music app: $12 in March, $12 in April
Bus fares: $30 in March, $22 in April
a.why: The music app cost the same amount in both months, so it is a fixed expense. Snacks, bus fares and clothes went up or down between months, so they are variable expenses, even though bus fares are paid often.
a.clue: Compare the two months for each item.

b.q: Jaden gets $200 a month from a weekend job. His fixed expenses are $60 and his variable expenses are $150. What does his budget show?
opts: A shortfall of $10, so he needs to cut expenses or earn more
$10 left over, so he can save $10 a month from his job
$140 left over, because only fixed expenses are counted
$50 left over, because only variable expenses are counted
b.why: Total expenses are $60 + $150 = $210, which is $10 more than his income of $200, so the budget shows a shortfall. The $140 and $50 answers each subtract only one kind of expense, but a budget counts both fixed and variable expenses.
b.clue: Add both kinds of expense before comparing with income.

a.best: Music app: $12 in March, $12 in April

b.best: A shortfall of $10, so he needs to cut expenses or earn more
